subject: Clarify token floor and rounding for Nimbus annual (streaming + long context)

Subject: Questions on token floor/rounding for annual contract

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a few clarifications before we sign the SOW:

1) How does Redwood handle "heartbeat" minimums vs per-call minimums — specifically for streaming calls that emit small deltas frequently? Do you apply a per-request minimum or a per-session floor?

2) For long-context calls (12k+ tokens) how does rounding work? If we send a 13,450-token prompt + 1,200-token generated output, is billing summed and rounded at the token level or are there separate buckets?

3) If we commit to a 500k token/month spend, what discount tier applies and are minimums waived/credited for the first quarter?

Procurement also requested an example invoice line showing how a month with 60% short streaming deltas and 40% long-context calls would be billed — ideally a simple spreadsheet.

I attached our draft SOW for context (SOW_Draft.docx). Can you point me to the exact language you expect in the contract around rounding/minimums so our legal can review?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Elena

Nimbus Health

Subject: Re: Questions on token floor/rounding for annual contract

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I attached an example invoice and a worked spreadsheet.

Short summary:
- Heartbeat / streaming deltas: we bill by token emitted, but we apply a per-call minimum of 50 tokens for short streaming RPCs by default. For long lived sessions we offer an alternative: a "session floor" (e.g., 1,500 tokens/session) that aggregates deltas during that session and applies one floor rather than many per-call minima.
- Long-context rounding: we sum prompt + output token counts per call and bill the total. Rounding is at the token unit, and we round up partial subtokens to whole tokens at tokenization time. There is no separate rounding step across buckets; totals are what matter on the invoice line.
- Commit discounts: 500k tokens/month falls into our mid-commit slab. Example: base list price -> 12% committed discount; we can carve in an introductory concession for Q1 (see options).

Attached: nimbus_pricing_example.xlsx (worked example for the traffic mix you described) and a draft SOW clause suggestion for rounding/minimums.

Options for you to consider:
A) Standard: Per-call minima (50 tokens), 12% committed discount at 500k token/mo, no upfront credit.
B) Pilot-friendly: Blended session floor (1,500 tokens/session for streaming-heavy workload), 12% discount, plus a one-month minimum credit applied after invoice (reduces first invoice to cover missed minimums).
C) Concession: 15% discount for a 12-month commit if procurement signs the attached SOW language with an explicit waiver of per-call minima for the first 90 days.

If you want, Ben can run the exact math and craft a redline for the SOW.

—Tessa

Subject: Re: Questions on token floor/rounding for annual contract — negotiation proposal

Kimberly / Tessa — looped in Marissa for ARR approval context. Notes and proposed language below that are safe for contract insertion but preserve product caveats: 

Proposed SOW paragraph (Option B variant, pilot-friendly):
"Redwood will apply a blended session floor for streaming RPCs during the pilot period. For streaming sessions, tokens emitted across a single session will be aggregated and a single session floor of 1,500 tokens will be applied per session in lieu of per-call minima. Tokens billed are the sum of tokenized prompt + tokenized response and are rounded up to whole tokens at tokenization time. Any session whose total tokens exceed the session floor is billed at actuals.

Redwood will provide token accounting logs (per-request token counts and timestamps) for a 90-day retention window for audit and reconciliation purposes.

For the pilot period (first 90 days), Redwood will apply a one-month invoice credit equal to the monthly minimum floor amount to reduce initial billing impact."

Commercial concession recommendation to offer procurement:
- 12% committed discount at 500k tokens/mo, plus one-month minimum credit applied on the second invoice.
- Alternatively, 15% for first 6 months, reverting to 12% thereafter if legal approves explicit waiver language.

Risk notes: session floors can inflate costs if customers open many short-lived sessions with low aggregate usage per session. Recommend we add an operational safety-net clause: "Redwood and Customer will monitor session averages during the first 30 days and may adjust session-floor thresholds if average session tokenization proves significantly below expected usage patterns."

If Kimberly gives green-light on the wording, I can bundle into a redline and hand to Legal for a quick review.

—Ben
